messages:
matt-ryan: heads up — seeing steady memory growth on longctx runs when we mix H100 + RTX nodes. suspect kvcache slot rotation is getting out of sync with the shadow page table; evict metrics spike but pt ownership sometimes points to a different GPU :thinking:

julia-ng: can you paste the minimal repro and a short trace? is this only with paged-attention workloads or with generic kv ops?

matt-ryan: repro is small-ish. command i used:
```
./tests/repro_longctx --model=long-2m --gpus=h100,rtx --seq=65536 --iters=1000 --log-interval=10
```
Behavior: memory keeps growing on gpu1, eviction count increases, but shadowmap shows entries owned by gpu0 while pt entries show gpu1. Attached a short excerpt of the debug dump below.

raj-patel: paste of the dump (filtered):
```
# time=1768001248 evict_count=42 pcie_stalls=1400us
shadowmap[0x1f4] = {owner: gpu0, epoch: 0x7e}
pt[0x1f4]        = {owner: gpu1, valid: 1, last_access: 1768001200}
shadowmap[0x1f5] = {owner: gpu1, epoch: 0x7f}
pt[0x1f5]        = {owner: gpu1, valid: 1}
# notice owner mismatch at 0x1f4
```

devin-cho: that looks like a stale shadow entry being used during slot rotation. do we update the pt and then rotate, or rotate then update? ordering bug could leave a window where evict reads the old shadow owner. also check for missing release/acquire between writes.

matt-ryan: current flow is: allocate slot -> write shadowmap(owner=) -> async PT update -> rotate index. i tried adding a release-store on the shadow write and an acquire-load before evict and saw the mismatch rate drop ~70% but not go away.

julia-ng: interesting. could be interaction with page-size alignment or chunking. are we using the same chunk_size on both GPUs? mixed CHUNKED_PAGE_SIZE was set to 2MB on H100 and 1MB on RTX in my quick env.

raj-patel: i reran with unified chunk size 2MB, and the repro changed shape: fewer owner mismatches but fragmentation grew faster — maybe the rotation math assumes uniform stride. log snippet:
```
slot_stride=4096 rotational_index=1023 -> wrap -> next_owner_lookup uses (rot_idx + 1) without mod safety
```

devin-cho: that line worries me. if rotation wraps and we compute next_owner using stale index and then do a non-atomic pt lookup, you can read the old mapping. could be a missing % num_slots or a signed/unsigned compare edge.

matt-ryan: added a quick guard for wrap and an extra atomic increment; this suppressed the immediate mismatch in my test but CI stress still showed intermittent leak after ~20k iters. attaching small perf counters: evict_latency histogram shifted right when mismatch occurs.

infra-bot: CI job triggered: r/eng-runtime#kvcache-pt-rotation-fix (run id: 4821). link: https://ci.internal/runs/4821

julia-ng: for debugging: can you dump both the raw GPU-side PT update trace and the CPU-side shadow writes with timestamps? i want to correlate the order. also enable ->trace=kvcache:owner-change

matt-ryan: will add timestamps. quick correlation shows cases where pt_update_ts < shadow_write_ts but reader sees pt after rotate, suggesting an ordering inversion on the bus (nvlink/nvlink+pcie mixed). hypothesis: writes to device memory from different buses can be observed out-of-order without an explicit barrier.

raj-patel: that matches a weirdness we saw with mixed NVLINK+PCIE topologies — we relied on implicit coherency but cross-bus visibility isn't strictly ordered. suggestion: add explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize or NVSHMEM fence around critical windows and see if it regresses perf but fixes correctness.

devin-cho: agree. also add a simple sequence-number stamp per slot so readers can detect torn updates: writer increments seq (odd while writing), writes data, increments seq (even) — reader checks seq even and matches before/after. cheap and avoids heavy fences in the fast path.

matt-ryan: i'll try seq-stamp first (low perf hit) then fallback to explicit fences. putting a small patch together on a branch and will drop logs.

julia-ng: assign to eng-runtime on Monday if CI confirms. add a short reproducer in tests/ so we can run in CI mixed-GPU matrix.

matt-ryan: thanks — i'll post the branch + logs here when ready. initial patch reduces mismatch frequency by ~95% locally. :thumbsup:

raj-patel: one more thing — check the PT caching layer's compaction path; if compaction moves slots concurrently you can get index aliasing. ensure compaction and rotation use the same global epoch.

matt-ryan: good call. adding compaction epoch sync to my checklist. will follow up with more traces.

infra-bot: reminder: please add test-case id kvcache-rot-001 when filing the bug.

matt-ryan: filed bug #INFR-2298 with initial repro and logs. assigning to devin/raj.

julia-ng: thanks team — good plan. we should check whether this needs a stable patch for Dedicated clusters (customer impact) or just a runtime fix.

matt-ryan: early impact seems low but reproducible under longctx stress. will escalate if CI shows regressions.
